en: I've lived in this city 63 years now,
running my optician's shop.
You'd look mighty fine in spectacles.
You ought to buy a pair.
Come back when the shop's open.
note: Starts a sentence in both uses (after #2994 'We're closed just now.' in 107717); same wording as #2995.

en: I'll have something you'll like
all ready for you.
No, I've no need of spectacles.
So this is an optician's.
Since before you were born, I've kept
this optician's shop.
I see. Well, well.
(The idea that I'm older than you
would never cross your mind...)
Welcome. Oh ho, you've come.
Now, what sort of spectacles will it be?
No, I really don't need spectacles.
Now, now, spectacles are a matter of style.
That's the very reason plain-glass spectacles
exist, you know.
Those pince-nez things
wouldn't suit me, I'm afraid.
Is that so? I think they'd suit you
Welcome. Spectacles
note: Cut off by #152 '...'; Warren starts his pitch, then recognises the player.

en: You don't need spectacles, as I recall.
Just wait a little longer.
An optician sells more than spectacles,
as I'll show you.
Now, this microscope. How about it?
No need for it? What a shame.
, how about this?
This lorgnette is all the rage in Vienna.
A cut above your common pince-nez.
Give it to a lady as a gift,
and she's sure to be grateful.
Oh? No ladies fond of spectacles in your
life, then?
Well, it can't be helped.
Well, well, thank you kindly.
That's the most fun I've had selling in ages.
Until the day you buy something,
I'm not giving up!
Warren
Laying my hands on someone like you
is painful, but
Your knowledge and skill as a craftsman
are sure to be useful.
How many people
must I lay hands on before it's enough
Lately, my scissors, I can't grip 'em right.
What's wrong with me
If you wish it, anything at all
Somehow, my body, it gets so tired.
I used to get around a lot more, I'm sure.
What is it?
I thought I would introduce myself.
I see. I'm Robin.
So long.
If that's all you want, go home.
You're not snooping on me because of
some weird rumour, are you?
Honestly, this is crazy.
Don't come in.
Oh, it's you. You can come in.
You already know my shop's secret, after all.
If my customers are gonna get a real shock,
the room's secret has to stay well hidden.
You get it, right?
But anyone who falls for it once is my friend.
Drop by any time.
It's our secret, hee hee.
I would like my hair trimmed.
Very, well.
note: Robin's polite speech is halting (#3115/#3116 say so); the JP comma is kept.

en: A customer, today, are you?
Is there, something, else?
My words, sound stiff, you think?
Polite talk, isn't my, strong point.
Lately, you hear lots of, scary rumours, right?
Hardly any of them are true, though.
Sit down right there.
